report: M1 Wayland scanout path review: wlroots puredarwin backend + PDGOP over IOGOPFramebuffer (software rendering, no GPU)
author_role: independent reviewer (Claude), read-only source review; no edits
verdict: The path is software rendering into the firmware framebuffer: pixman renders, then the puredarwin backend memcpy's rows into IOGOP's VRAM mapped through PDGOP. Ownership hand-off and user-client selectors are correct. Two concrete fixes are needed for correct M1 output, plus one recommended: (W1, required) the backend ignores pixel format and copies XRGB8888 raw into the 2101010 framebuffer, giving wrong colours; (W2, required/recommended) the VRAM user mapping is not write-combined on arm64 unless the framebuffer sets 'pd-vram-write-combine', which IOGOP never does, so it defaults to Device memory: slow, with an alignment-fault risk for unaligned stores; (W3, optional) the kernel IOFramebuffer VRAM map is InhibitCache on arm64. No GPU, vblank, mode-setting or hardware cursor is involved or claimed.
path_as_built: sway.nix sets WLR_BACKENDS=puredarwin and WLR_RENDERER=pixman by default; wlroots.nix builds -Dbackends=puredarwin -Drenderers=[] (pixman only, no GLES/Vulkan).

backend.c: PDSurfaceDeviceOpen and pd_virgl_open only find IOVirtIOGPU (PDSurface.c provider list), so on M1 both are absent: gpu == NULL, and the PureDarwin allocator declines => shm buffers and the copy path.
output.c puredarwin_output_create -> PDGOPOpen; output mode = framebuffer width x height, custom 60 Hz; 16 ms timer as the frame source (no vblank).

PDGOPOpen: matches IOVirtIOGPU, then IOGOPFramebuffer, then IOFramebuffer; IOServiceOpen type 0 (kIOFBServerConnectType); selector 2 extGetCurrentDisplayMode and selector 1 extGetPixelInformation (match IOFramebufferUserClient methodTemplate); maps kIOFBVRAMMemory (110 = IOGraphicsTypesPrivate.h). It stores width/height/stride/bpp/pixelType/masks[0..2], but not bitsPerComponent or the pixelFormat string.

output_commit copy path: memcpy of max_width*4 bytes per row from the wlroots buffer to the VRAM mapping, ignoring the buffer's DRM format and the framebuffer masks; pd_virgl_present only when gpu != NULL.

findings.title: pixel format mismatch: XRGB8888 copied raw into XRGB2101010 storage
findings.fact: With framebuffer-30bit.patch, PDGOP receives bpp 32 and masks 3ff00000/000ffc00/000003ff. The backend implements no get_primary_formats, so wlroots treats the output as able to display any format (output.c wlr_output_get_primary_formats returns NULL; render.c output_pick_format copies the render format) and uses the default render format DRM_FORMAT_XRGB8888 (types/output/output.c:354). The commit path then copies 8888 words unchanged into 2101010 storage: geometry is right (4 bytes/px), colours are wrong (each 10-bit field takes the wrong bit spans).
findings.minimal_fix: In the puredarwin backend only: (a) derive the framebuffer fourcc from PDGOP bpp + masks: (32, 00ff0000/0000ff00/000000ff) => DRM_FORMAT_XRGB8888; (32, 3ff00000/000ffc00/000003ff) => DRM_FORMAT_XRGB2101010; anything else => fail output creation with an explicit log, never guess. (b) Implement output get_primary_formats for WLR_BUFFER_CAP_DATA_PTR returning that fourcc (MOD_INVALID/LINEAR), and set the initial output render format to it (wlr_output_state_set_render_format before wlr_output_init), so the pixman renderer (which supports DRM_FORMAT_XRGB2101010 <-> PIXMAN_x2r10g10b10, pixel_format.c:88) renders native 2101010 and the existing row memcpy becomes correct. (c) In output_commit, memcpy only when the buffer format equals the framebuffer fourcc; if a compositor forces XRGB8888/ARGB8888 onto a 2101010 framebuffer, convert per pixel (8->10-bit expansion v10 = v<<2 | v>>6) or reject the commit with an error. No silent raw copy across formats.

findings.severity: required for usable output (recommended at minimum)
findings.title: VRAM user mapping is not write-combined on arm64
findings.fact: IOFramebufferUserClient clientMemoryForType(kIOFBVRAMMemory) adds kIOMapWriteCombineCache on arm64 only if the framebuffer has the property 'pd-vram-write-combine'; nothing in the tree sets it (grep: only the reader). The framebuffer PA lies outside XNU-managed RAM, so pmap_cache_attributes returns VM_WIMG_IO unless ADT pmap-io-ranges says otherwise, and the default user mapping is Device memory. Consequences (source reasoning, not executed): every full-frame copy (2560x1600x4 = 16 MB per commit) runs at Device-memory store speed, and any unaligned or overlapping store a libc memmove may emit (or a partial-row/damage copy) can alignment-fault. The kernel's own console mapping of the same buffer is VM_WIMG_WCOMB (initialize_screen, HAS_UCNORMAL_MEM).
findings.minimal_fix: IOGOPFramebuffer sets property 'pd-vram-write-combine' = true for the firmware boot framebuffer (DRAM scanned by DCP; WC is the attribute the kernel console already uses), via the existing opt-in hook; no IOGraphics change. Separate from framebuffer-30bit.patch; it needs its own patch/review/build.

findings.title: kernel IOFramebuffer VRAM map is InhibitCache on arm64
findings.fact: IOFramebuffer.cpp kIOFBMapCacheMode = kIOMapInhibitCache on non-x86, and fVramMap (used for newConsole.v_baseAddr at the console handoff) is mapped with it. After the handoff the kernel text console therefore paints and scrolls (video_scroll_up reads) through a Device mapping, which is slow but functionally consistent with display-010's buffer readback.
findings.option: Honour 'pd-vram-write-combine' for the kernel fVramMap too. Not required for Wayland correctness.

findings.title: ownership hand-off
findings.fact: IOServiceOpen type 0 => IOFramebuffer::newUserClient(kIOFBServerConnectType) => setPlatformConsole(0, kPEReleaseScreen) when this is the console framebuffer => gc_enable(FALSE): the kernel console stops painting while the compositor owns VRAM. disableConsoleOutput stays FALSE because serialmode has SERIALMODE_OUTPUT, so the UART mirror continues. A second server connection gets kIOReturnExclusiveAccess. On close, IOFramebuffer calls setPlatformConsole(0, kPEAcquireScreen) (console resume; Astra owns that owner-state patch).

findings.title: PDGOPPresent is a virtio-only selector
findings.fact: PDGOPPresent calls selector 11 (kPDGPU_Present, virtio user client). On an IOGOP IOFramebufferUserClient, selector 11 is extSetGammaTable (expects 5 scalars), so the call fails argument validation (bad argument), with no gamma change. The wlroots IOGOP path does not call it; xf86-video-puredarwingop does (puredarwingop_drv.c:466). Gate it on the IOVirtIOGPU service class.

findings.title: input
findings.fact: The backend reads /dev/usb_hid_kbd and /dev/usb_hid_mouse (PDHIDEventQueue in IOHIDFamily). On M1 there is no internal-keyboard/trackpad driver in this tree; PDSerialHID ('listening for SOH lines on the serial console', attempt-006 log) is the only plausible source today. Not verified end-to-end.

findings.title: full-frame copies on one CPU
findings.fact: The copy path rewrites the whole 16 MB frame per commit by design (virtio drift note) on a single CPU (cpus=1) under the HV; plus pixman rendering of 2560x1600. Damage-limited copies for the IOGOP (non-virtio) case would cut this; not needed for correctness.

findings.title: scale and physical size
findings.fact: There is no EDID or physical size and the boot framebuffer is 2x (retina); compositor config should set output scale 2. No real vblank: the 16 ms timer can tear.

no_gpu_claim: Everything above is CPU/pixman rendering into the iBoot-initialized framebuffer that DCP already scans out. No AGX/GPU, display controller programming, mode set, vblank or hardware cursor is involved.
relation_to_display_010: Root reports display-010 attempt-001 framebuffer readback (decoded buffer image, not a physical panel photo) contains the shell prompt and fresh nonce matching serial; that concerns the kernel console path (W3 applies to it), not this Wayland path.
